title: The base change map of the structure sheaf is a morphism of algebras
statement: Let $f:X\to S$, $f':X'\to S'$, $g:S'\to S$, $g':X'\to X$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $f\circ g'=g\circ f'$, let $g^*\dashv g_*$ etc. be the pullback and pushforward of modules [def-pc-module-pullback] with units $\eta$, and let $\otimes$ be the tensor product of modules [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal A'=f'_*\mathcal O_{X'}$ with their algebra structures (sections $\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}W)$, multiplications $\mu:\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$, $\mu'$, units $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal A$, $f'^\sharp:\mathcal O_{S'}\to\mathcal A'$). Give $g^*\mathcal A$ the multiplication $g^*(\mu)\circ t^{-1}:g^*\mathcal A\otimes g^*\mathcal A\to g^*\mathcal A$, with $t:g^*(\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A)\cong g^*\mathcal A\otimes g^*\mathcal A$ the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor], and the unit $g^*(f^\sharp)\circ\epsilon_g^{-1}:\mathcal O_{S'}\to g^*\mathcal A$, with $\epsilon_g:g^*\mathcal O_S\cong\mathcal O_{S'}$ and $\epsilon_{g'}:g'^*\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_{X'}$ the isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. Let $\beta:g^*\mathcal A\to f'_*g'^*\mathcal O_X$ be the base change map, i.e. the morphism corresponding under $g^*\dashv g_*$ to $f_*(\eta_{g',\mathcal O_X}):f_*\mathcal O_X\to f_*g'_*g'^*\mathcal O_X=g_*f'_*g'^*\mathcal O_X$, and $\gamma=f'_*(\epsilon_{g'})\circ\beta:g^*\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$. Then (i) $\gamma$ is the morphism corresponding under $g^*\dashv g_*$ to $f_*(g'^\sharp):\mathcal A\to g_*\mathcal A'$, i.e. $\gamma(\eta_g(a))=g'^\sharp(a)\in\mathcal O_{X'}(f'^{-1}g^{-1}W)$ for $a\in\mathcal A(W)=\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}W)$; (ii) $\gamma\circ g^*(\mu)=\mu'\circ(\gamma\otimes\gamma)\circ t$ and $\gamma\circ g^*(f^\sharp)=f'^\sharp\circ\epsilon_g$, i.e. $\gamma$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_{S'}$-algebras. (No hypothesis on $f$ or on the square beyond commutativity.)

source.place: not stated in the Stacks project: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02KG gives only the module isomorphism; the creator of lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change derived the algebra compatibility affine-locally; this node states it for any commutative square (base change map of Cohomology, Remark 08HY, literature/stacks-project/cohomology.tex)

proof.text: *(1) Conventions.* For a morphism of schemes $h:Y\to Z$, the adjunction $h^*\dashv h_*$ of [def-pc-module-pullback] with unit $\eta_h$ gives the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Y}(h^*\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Z}(\mathcal M,h_*\mathcal N)$, $\psi\mapsto h_*(\psi)\circ\eta_{h,\mathcal M}$ (Stacks, Sheaves, Lemma 008Z); in particular two morphisms $\psi_1,\psi_2:h^*\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ are equal as soon as $h_*(\psi_1)\circ\eta_{h,\mathcal M}=h_*(\psi_2)\circ\eta_{h,\mathcal M}$. The unit is natural: $h_*h^*(u)\circ\eta_{h,\mathcal M}=\eta_{h,\mathcal M'}\circ u$ for $u:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'$. On sections, $(h_*\mathcal N)(W)=\mathcal N(h^{-1}W)$ and $h_*(\psi)_W=\psi_{h^{-1}W}$. For $a\in\mathcal M(W)$ write $h^*a=\eta_{h,\mathcal M}(a)\in(h^*\mathcal M)(h^{-1}W)$; then $\psi(h^*a)=(h_*(\psi)\circ\eta_{h,\mathcal M})(a)$. Since $f\circ g'=g\circ f'$ [def-pc-scheme], $f_*g'_*=g_*f'_*$ on sheaves (sections over $W$ are sections over $g'^{-1}f^{-1}W=f'^{-1}g^{-1}W$, and the same on morphisms), and the two $\mathcal O_S$-module structures agree because $f_*(g'^\sharp)\circ f^\sharp=(f\circ g')^\sharp=(g\circ f')^\sharp=g_*(f'^\sharp)\circ g^\sharp$ (composition of morphisms of ringed spaces, Stacks, Sheaves, Definition 0093); this identification is used without comment below. These are the definitions and the formal properties of an adjunction.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 008Z (sheaves-lemma-adjoint-pull-push-modules: g^* left adjoint to g_* on modules) and Definition 0093 (sheaves-definition-composition-maps-ringed-spaces: (f\circ g')^\sharp=f_*(g'^\sharp)\circ f^\sharp); the argument itself is not in the Stacks project (agent-written)

proof.text:
*(2) Part (i).* By definition of $\beta$ (step (1) with $h=g$), $g_*(\beta)\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal A}=f_*(\eta_{g',\mathcal O_X})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf], $g'_*(\epsilon_{g'})\circ\eta_{g',\mathcal O_X}=g'^\sharp$. Hence
$$g_*(\gamma)\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal A}=g_*f'_*(\epsilon_{g'})\circ g_*(\beta)\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal A}=f_*g'_*(\epsilon_{g'})\circ f_*(\eta_{g',\mathcal O_X})=f_*\big(g'_*(\epsilon_{g'})\circ\eta_{g',\mathcal O_X}\big)=f_*(g'^\sharp),$$
so $\gamma$ is the morphism corresponding to $f_*(g'^\sharp):\mathcal A\to f_*g'_*\mathcal O_{X'}=g_*\mathcal A'$. Evaluated on $a\in\mathcal A(W)=\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}W)$ (step (1)): $\gamma(g^*a)=f_*(g'^\sharp)(a)=g'^\sharp_{f^{-1}W}(a)\in\mathcal O_{X'}(g'^{-1}f^{-1}W)=\mathcal O_{X'}(f'^{-1}g^{-1}W)$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 008Z (sheaves-lemma-adjoint-pull-push-modules: g^* left adjoint to g_* on modules) and Definition 0093 (sheaves-definition-composition-maps-ringed-spaces: (f\circ g')^\sharp=f_*(g'^\sharp)\circ f^\sharp); the argument itself is not in the Stacks project (agent-written)

proof.text: *(3) Multiplications.* Both $\gamma\circ g^*(\mu)$ and $\mu'\circ(\gamma\otimes\gamma)\circ t$ are $\mathcal O_{S'}$-linear maps $g^*(\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A)\to\mathcal A'$ ($\gamma\otimes\gamma$ the induced map of tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the sheafification of $s\otimes s'\mapsto\gamma(s)\otimes\gamma(s')$, so $(\gamma\otimes\gamma)(s\otimes s')=\gamma(s)\otimes\gamma(s')$ on sections). By step (1) it suffices to show that their adjoints $\Phi_1=g_*(\gamma\circ g^*(\mu))\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A}$ and $\Phi_2=g_*(\mu'\circ(\gamma\otimes\gamma)\circ t)\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A}$, $\mathcal O_S$-linear maps $\mathcal A\otimes_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal A\to g_*\mathcal A'$, are equal. The sheaf $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A$ is the sheafification of the presheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and $g_*\mathcal A'$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_S$-modules, so by the uniqueness in the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] it suffices that $\Phi_1$ and $\Phi_2$ agree after composition with $\mathcal A\otimes_p\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A$, i.e. on the images of the elements $a\otimes b$, $a,b\in\mathcal A(W)$, $W\subseteq S$ open, which generate $\mathcal A(W)\otimes_{\mathcal O_S(W)}\mathcal A(W)$ as an abelian group. By naturality of the unit, $\Phi_1=g_*(\gamma)\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal A}\circ\mu=f_*(g'^\sharp)\circ\mu$ (step (2)), so $\Phi_1(a\otimes b)=g'^\sharp(ab)$. On the other side, $\eta_{g,\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A}(a\otimes b)=g^*(a\otimes b)$, which $t$ sends to $g^*a\otimes g^*b$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor]; $\gamma\otimes\gamma$ sends this to $\gamma(g^*a)\otimes\gamma(g^*b)=g'^\sharp(a)\otimes g'^\sharp(b)$ (step (2)), and $\mu'$ to the product $g'^\sharp(a)\,g'^\sharp(b)$ in $\mathcal O_{X'}(f'^{-1}g^{-1}W)$. So $\Phi_2(a\otimes b)=g'^\sharp(a)g'^\sharp(b)=g'^\sharp(ab)=\Phi_1(a\otimes b)$, because $g'^\sharp_{f^{-1}W}:\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}W)\to\mathcal O_{X'}(g'^{-1}f^{-1}W)$ is a ring homomorphism ($g'$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]). Hence $\gamma\circ g^*(\mu)=\mu'\circ(\gamma\otimes\gamma)\circ t$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 008Z (sheaves-lemma-adjoint-pull-push-modules: g^* left adjoint to g_* on modules) and Definition 0093 (sheaves-definition-composition-maps-ringed-spaces: (f\circ g')^\sharp=f_*(g'^\sharp)\circ f^\sharp); the argument itself is not in the Stacks project (agent-written)

proof.text: *(4) Units.* Both $\gamma\circ g^*(f^\sharp)$ and $f'^\sharp\circ\epsilon_g$ are $\mathcal O_{S'}$-linear maps $g^*\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal A'$; by step (1) it suffices to compare their adjoints. By naturality of the unit and step (2), $g_*(\gamma\circ g^*(f^\sharp))\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal O_S}=g_*(\gamma)\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal A}\circ f^\sharp=f_*(g'^\sharp)\circ f^\sharp=(f\circ g')^\sharp$. By the defining property of $\epsilon_g$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf], $g_*(f'^\sharp\circ\epsilon_g)\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal O_S}=g_*(f'^\sharp)\circ g^\sharp=(g\circ f')^\sharp$. These agree as $f\circ g'=g\circ f'$ (step (1)). Hence $\gamma\circ g^*(f^\sharp)=f'^\sharp\circ\epsilon_g$, i.e. $\gamma$ sends the unit $g^*(f^\sharp)\circ\epsilon_g^{-1}$ of $g^*\mathcal A$ to the unit $f'^\sharp$ of $\mathcal A'$. With step (3) and the $\mathcal O_{S'}$-linearity of $\gamma$ (it is a morphism of $\mathcal O_{S'}$-modules by construction), $\gamma$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_{S'}$-algebras; this proves (ii).
